answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by tying standing to continuous liveness on a unique channel, spot-checked at random. The ledger swings its lantern randomly; each identity answers through its single-serving line before a hard deadline, or its stake is slashed. A sybil cannot time-share one line across a reef of clones: checks are unsynchronized and a line serves one response once, so each clone needs its channel, a linear non-shareable cost. Clones swarm for the nectar of reward, yet each rents its line. A rich attacker can still buy many lines, so it caps cheap cloning, not wealth.
